## Context

`basicly-e2mz.46` absorbs two research documents into the architecture and is **blocked**: it is
ordered last of four `architecture.md` writers and two of them (`basicly-vkh0.42.6`,
`basicly-1hp91f`) are still open. Meanwhile the rule that binds that absorption, architecture
D-36, says an absorbed *Because* inherits a measurement that can expire, so it is **re-run or it
is not absorbed**.

`docs/research/2026-07-26-sota-review.md` is dated 27 days before today. `docs/research/2026-08-17-deepseek-harness.md` pins `il-ai/il-harness` at `dsh-0.1.0-rc.8`, verified 2026-08-20. Both hold numbers `e2mz.46` would have to carry.

This record does the half that has no scope collision: it re-measures the evidence, so that when
the architecture.md chain clears, `e2mz.46` carries dated facts rather than expired ones. It
writes only `docs/research/`. It does not touch `architecture.md` and does not decide adoption.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a claim in either research document carries a number, THE RE-MEASUREMENT SHALL restate it against the current source and SHALL record the date it was verified at.
- WHEN a re-measured number differs from the recorded one, THE DOCUMENT SHALL carry both, the delta, and the command that produced the new figure.
- WHEN a pinned upstream version has moved, THE DOCUMENT SHALL record the new pin, the old pin, and what changed between them.
- WHEN a claim cannot be re-measured, IT SHALL be named as unverifiable with the reason, rather than restated.
- WHERE a research claim merely restates shipped basicly code, IT SHALL be marked droppable so the absorption drops rather than moves it.

## Scope

- `docs/research/2026-07-26-sota-review.md`
- `docs/research/2026-08-17-deepseek-harness.md`

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Read the refreshed evidence table and check that every row carries a verified-at date no older than today, and that each changed figure names the command that produced it.

payload.description:
## Context

`uv run basicly tracker write -- update basicly-nonexistent` prints `recorded: update basicly-nonexistent`
and exits zero. No event reaches the ledger and no record is created - verified, so nothing is corrupted
- but the operator is told a write happened.

Measured 2026-08-20: `tracker show basicly-nonexistent` answers `"found": false`, and
`grep -c basicly-nonexistent .basicly/ledger/events-*.jsonl` returns 0, against a record count unchanged
at 984.

The cost is a false confirmation on the one surface an operator uses to check their own work. A typo in
a record id during a batch of updates is silently accepted, and the only way to notice is to read the
record back. Compare `dep remove`, which `basicly-he6200` deliberately made refuse an absent edge for
exactly this reason.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `uv run basicly tracker write -- update basicly-nonexistent`.
2. Observe `recorded: update basicly-nonexistent` and exit zero.
3. Run `uv run basicly tracker show basicly-nonexistent` and observe `found: false`.
4. Run `grep -c basicly-nonexistent .basicly/ledger/events-*.jsonl` and observe 0.
5. Run the same update against a record that exists and observe the same message, which is the positive control that the message does not discriminate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an update naming a record the tracker does not hold when the write runs then it is refused naming the id rather than reported as recorded - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_mirror.py -k update_absent -q`
- Given an update naming a record that exists then it is recorded unchanged

## Scope

- `src/basicly/owned_write.py`
- `tests/test_mirror.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/owned_write.py`
- `tests/test_mirror.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_mirror.py -k update_absent -q`

## Context

Decided by the orchestrator, 2026-11-12, outside the M5 core. basicly-gtb19bg.43.13 keeps a retracted tip as a local ref and refuses shares until fsck --vault --repair runs. Between the retraction and the repair, another writer's lost lines live on this machine only in that ref.

## Goal

Close that window: the fetch that finds a retraction runs the repair at once.

## Acceptance

- When a fetch finds that the head lacks the seen tip, the tracker shall run the repair in the same command when its deadline allows, else keep the current refusal.
- Proof: input a clone that saw a commit later removed by a force-push; action one fetch with no deadline; pass when the lost lines are queued and the next share succeeds without a separate repair.

## Risk

A hook fetch has a 3 s deadline. A repair needs a full chain check and can take longer; the fetch must then fall back to the refusal and never block the agent.

payload.description:
## Context

`.basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py` records a skill only when the Claude `Skill` tool is
invoked (`_skill_from_payload` requires `tool.lower() == "skill"`). Skills attached through
an agent definition's `skills:` frontmatter passthrough are *preloaded*, not invoked, so they
fire no `Skill` call and are invisible to the counter.

Consequence: `basicly usage report` lists them under "Never-used catalog skills (culling
candidates)". On 2026-08-13 that list named `decompose-plan`, `repair-in-place`,
`validate-as-consumer` and `root-cause` - which are exactly the four skills declared in the
engine's own agent frontmatter (`.claude/agents/decomposer.md`, `implementer.md`,
`validator.md`, `researcher.md`, `retrospector.md`).

The report invites culling on this list, so the instrument actively recommends deleting the
skills the engine depends on. Only the never-used side of a usage audit can be manufactured
by a measurement bug, which is why this one is worth fixing rather than annotating.

Unresolved and worth settling in the same unit: whether the host honours the `skills:`
passthrough at all. `agents.py:372` calls it deliberately untyped, "its shape is the host's
to define", and nothing in the repo asserts it is honoured. If it is not, the four agents
are running without the skills they declare and nobody would see it.

## Proposed check

Either count a preloaded skill at dispatch time from the agent definition, or exclude
frontmatter-declared skills from the never-used list and say why in the report. Whichever is
chosen, a test must show a preloaded skill does not appear as a culling candidate.
payload.title: Record a preloaded skill so the usage audit stops inventing never used

payload.text: Resolved by basicly-ey58 (shipped 2026-08-13, beb7f01). The open half of this bead was whether skills: has a defined shape; it does - a documented, typed list of skill names - and the defect was the spawn mode, not the schema. agents.py's 'deliberately untyped (its shape is the host's to define)' is refuted. The engine now reads the declared bodies and carries them in the dispatch prompt for every family, so the field has a runtime effect and catalog_lint's skill/role pairing enforces something real.

payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-23 on the basicly-k6tpep supervise session launched with --tier medium under an L3 110M grant. At the first ship checkpoint the engine declined the grant's delegation with: 'L3 grant cannot be metered: 1 dispatch(es) under it reported no measurable usage, so only a chars/4 floor over their captured output exists (514323 estimated, far below real spend) and 54598042/110000000 tokens is not what this grant has cost; the session is human-only until re-granted or the runner is configured with a usage format' (decision basicly-ze0po3#ec15dfaca8). The decline is correct behaviour - an unmeterable grant must not self-approve - but the cause is that a dispatch under a tier override emits usage the meter does not parse, so every checkpoint of an otherwise autonomous session returns to a human. The prior unmeterable case (the decider dispatch) was fixed 2026-08-03; this is the tier-override variant.

## Steps to Reproduce

Grant L3 with a token budget on an epic, run basicly loop supervise <epic> --tier medium, let one lane finish and reach ship. The grant declines with the cannot-be-metered message.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane dispatches under a --tier override, THE RUN RECORD SHALL carry measured usage in the same format as a default-tier dispatch, or name the model whose stream lacked it.
- WHEN every dispatch under a grant carries measured usage, THE GRANT SHALL remain delegable for checkpoints.
- WHEN a dispatch reports no measurable usage, THE DECLINE MESSAGE SHALL name the dispatch and the model so the operator can fix the runner configuration rather than guess.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
- `tests/test_run_record.py`

payload.description:
## Finding
Reported by the handily session on 2026-11-16 at 15:10 UTC and reproduced by the basicly session.
A fresh install of released 0.46.1 in an empty repository refuses its own first commit.
The pre-commit catalog lint prints:

    catalog lint: FAILED
      .basicly/core/skills/agent-mail/skill.yaml: model-invoked skill 'agent-mail' is declared by no agent, so the engine inlines it into no dispatch prompt and the guidance reaches no role; add it to an agent's claude.skills, or — if no role should carry it — to skill_pairing.UNPAIRED_EXEMPTIONS with the reason

## Reproduction
Scratch folder, scratch HOME, normal PATH that holds a global basicly 0.45.0 (uv tool install).

    git init -q -b main
    printf '[hooks.markdownlint]\nenabled = false\n' > basicly.toml
    uvx --python '>=3.14' --from https://github.com/niksavis/basicly/releases/download/v0.46.1/basicly-0.46.1-py3-none-any.whl basicly install
    git add -A
    git commit -m 'chore: install basicly'

Install exits 0 with 'repo converged'. The commit exits 1 with the output above.

## Control
Same repository and commit, PATH without the global basicly, uv and uvx still reachable.
The commit exits 0 and prints 'catalog lint: OK'. The hook then used the uvx 0.46.1 wheel.

## Cause
.basicly/core/hooks/catalog-lint.py _cli_command takes shutil.which('basicly') first.
It uses the install-state version (uvx from dist_source) only when no basicly is on PATH.
A global basicly 0.45.0 lints the 0.46.1 catalog.
The agent-mail skill and its UNPAIRED_EXEMPTIONS entry in src/basicly/skill_pairing.py first shipped in v0.46.0 (c5d9ebf5).
So the older engine does not know the exemption and refuses.
Main at fb6c2341 has the same fault: the hook body is unchanged since v0.46.1.
tracker-fold.py and session-start.py also take shutil.which('basicly') first and may share the skew.

## Impact
Every consumer with an older global basicly fails the first commit after an install or upgrade.
Onboarding of development, basicly, handily and terminal starts from a fresh install, so this blocks it.
Separate, not fixed here: install refuses at once without markdownlint and writes nothing; the documented opt-out was used.

payload.description:
## Trigger
The owner asked whether the published page had been updated, 2026-09-12, after v0.13.0 shipped.

## What was already right
The release rewrote the install pin, the pages workflow deployed on the release commit, and the live page shows v0.13.0. The page also names two agent skill roots rather than three, so it carried none of the stale claim the changelog did.

## The defect
The Guidance pillar reads "One versioned YAML catalog, projected into what each tool natively reads: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions.md, skills, subagents, permissions." That enumeration is the claim, and output styles became a seventh projected type in this same release. The list went out one short.

## Why no gate caught it
`site/index.html` is a declared consumer surface in `docs_claim_surfaces.py`, but `docs-claims` reads commands and generated blocks. Nothing binds a prose enumeration of projected types to the set the projector actually writes.

## What I nearly broke while fixing it
I also added output styles to the diagram aria-label. The figure draws five output boxes and has none for output styles, so the label would have described something not on screen. Reverted; a screen-reader label has to match the figure, and the figure is a deliberate simplification.

## Worth considering, not filed as work
The enumeration is derivable: the projector knows every output type it writes. A generated block would keep the sentence true for free, the way the always-on size table already works.

## Scope
- `site/index.html`

## Context

Second read-only survey on 2026-08-26, over the architecture sections basicly-byvpvx did not reach (§1, §4-§16, §18-§21, §26.3-4, §29.2-4, §31, §32, §34, §35, §36.3-6, §36.8, §37, §39). Ten claims are refuted by the code, each CONFIRMED by reading the symbol. Seven of the ten are hand-typed counts that the tree already publishes through a gated generated block or a CLI listing; the rule that follows is: a count the tree prints is never typed into the document, it is deleted or bound.

1. §16 line ~941/949: "15 declared specs", pre-tool-use row lists 2 hooks. `.basicly/core/hooks/hooks.yaml:82` declares `unsplit-loop-guard` (pretooluse, claude): 16 specs, pretooluse 3 (`protect-generated`, `unsplit-loop-guard`, `pipe-status-guard`), claude routes 4. Fix: delete both tables; point at the gated block `catalog-hooks` in `.basicly/core/hooks/README.md`.
2. §34 line ~3324: "The two dashed self-edges are the only exceptions". `.importlinter` has one `ignore_imports` (`basicly.policy -> basicly.decisions`); `.scripts/docs_claim_layers.py:248-255` draws one dashed edge. Fix: rewrite to the singular, or emit the sentence from `docs_claim_layers.py` so it pluralises from `exemptions()`.
3. §13 line ~744: "path-scoped fragments | 4". Six sources carry non-default `scope.paths`; `.claude/rules/` holds 6 files. §12.2's codex-cap argument rests on this count. Fix: delete the row or bind it to `len(glob('.claude/rules/*.md'))` in `.scripts/docs_claims.py`.
4. §6 line ~351: "Redaction runs at the write seam of both stores." `src/basicly/owned_store.py:44` `TRACKER_MODES = (MODE_OWNED,)`; one `events.append(..., redact=...)` in `tracker.py:528`. §35 says "the whole store". Fix: "Redaction runs at the tracker's write seam."
5. §5 line ~306/309: catalog is "data, never code"; "`.basicly/` never holds engine code." `.basicly/core/hooks/*.py` (16 scripts) and `.basicly/core/kit/{tracker,tier}/` (19 modules) are code by design; §10.1 and §32 say so. Fix: "authored data plus the portable hook and kit scripts; never engine modules", and "`.basicly/` never holds `basicly` engine modules" (the `kit-boundary` gate is the real rule).
6. §39 line ~4870 and §32.8 line ~3043: "`comments add` ... until the flip removes it". `src/basicly/mirror.py:40` and `write_verbs.py:275-289` still mint `KIND_COMMENT`; §37.3 records the flip as ran. Fix: present tense, "which the translator still turns into a `comment` event"; drop "until the flip removes it".
7. §13 line ~741: "core fragments | 21". 23 sources, 22 active. Fix: delete the table; `basicly catalog list fragment` is the answer.
8. §14 line ~847: "skill sources | 41". 42 directories. Fix: delete; point at the gated block `catalog-skills` in `.basicly/core/skills/README.md`.
9. §15 line ~857/922 and §30 line ~2192: "Four shared blocks". Five in `.basicly/core/agents/blocks/`. Fix: delete the count table and the diagram literal, or bind in `tests/test_docs_drift.py` (byvpvx finding 9 covers the §30 site; do not edit §30 here).
10. §26.3 line ~1683: "The limit is floored at two." `src/basicly/retrospective.py:76` `MIN_SPECIAL_COUNT = 2` floors the observed failure count, not the control limit (`:142-143`, `centre + 3*sqrt(centre)`, no floor). Fix: "A point carrying fewer than two failures can never signal, whatever the limit says (`retrospective.MIN_SPECIAL_COUNT`)."

Verified correct: §9.1-2, §12.1 caps, §14 `--all-default-roots`, §32.3 ten of eighteen kinds, §37.3, §36.8 workflows, §36.7 six blocks, §34 generated layering block, §20 append-only exception, §21 install artifacts. Not probed at code depth: §7 instruments, §31.2-5 arithmetic, §29.2-4 metering, §32.4-10, §18 deny semantics, §26.4, §31.6, §36.3, §36.6.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN each finding is applied, THE DOCUMENT SHALL state what the cited code does, and `uv run python .scripts/docs_claims.py --check`, `uv run pytest tests/test_docs_drift.py tests/test_docs_claims.py -q` SHALL pass.
- WHEN a finding is a count (1, 3, 7, 8, 9), THE DOCUMENT SHALL either not carry the number or carry it inside a generated block or under a tripwire, so the next drift fails a gate.
- WHEN the record closes, ITS CLOSING COMMENT SHALL name the sections not probed at code depth.

## Scope

- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `.scripts/docs_claims.py`
- `.scripts/docs_claim_layers.py`
- `tests/test_docs_claims.py`
- `tests/test_docs_drift.py`

payload.description:
When install finishes in a repository that already excludes the managed core from its linters, I want it to say nothing, so I can stop training a consumer to skim the region where a tracked CI edit is also reported.

Found by the terminal canary, filed there as term-ip2wz and pressed after it shipped twice unchanged. scaffolds.install_notes tests only whether a config file exists, never what it contains, so it advises extend-exclude on a .ruff.toml that has carried exactly that for releases. The canary verified the exclusion is genuinely in force rather than merely present: ruff format --check over the managed core exits 0 on 54 files.

The same block tells a consumer to hand-edit .pre-commit-config.yaml in a run that separately reports it has just rewritten that file.

Severity is low and nothing fails. The reason it is worth fixing is where it sits: the advice is the tail of the install output, and the tail is also where a re-pin of a tracked CI workflow is announced. Unactionable boilerplate beside a real edit teaches a reader to skip both.

Recorded against myself: this was already a requirement on basicly-fmgwtwi, which is still open, and I shipped two releases without meeting it while telling the canary it was on the record. It was on the record and it was not done.
payload.requirements: the check reads the file rather than testing its presence. A false skip is possible if the path is named for some other reason, and that is accepted and stated rather than guarded, because the cost of a missed note is one line a consumer can still read in the documentation.
payload.title: read the file before advising a change it already carries

payload.title: Basicly-tracker crashes on Windows when it writes JSON with non-cp1252 characters to a pipe

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
When basicly-tracker writes JSON to a pipe on a cp1252 host, it shall write UTF-8 and exit 0.
When the payload holds a character outside cp1252, the output shall parse as JSON with the character unchanged.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
When a program runs basicly-tracker on Windows and reads its stdout through a pipe, I want valid UTF-8 JSON, so I can parse the output on any host.

Reported on 2026-10-09 from Windows 11, Python 3.14, basicly-tracker 0.21.5: list through subprocess.run(capture_output=True) exits 1 with UnicodeEncodeError in cp1252, from kit cli.py print(json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False)). On a pipe Python encodes stdout with the locale. Reproduced on Linux with PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252: kit list exits 1. The engine basicly tracker reads use the same print, and the engine sets errors=replace, so it would print a question mark in place of the character. Caller workaround: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a consumer shapes a record for an agent to verify against, I want the gate to read one store rather than two, so I can stop the disagreement D-50 was written to end.

D-50 decided that acceptance_criteria and requirements are fields and not headings, that the field becomes the only reader, and that the heading survives only as a read-only fallback for a closed record and is refused for an open one. The shaping module shipped in basicly-b84ql8z accepts a heading on any record. Measured 2026-09-18: a heading-only open record owes nothing, so the gate passes it.

I built that fallback deliberately for backward compatibility and did not check it against the decision before doing so. D-50's own argument applies to the kit unchanged: two representations of one truth is a disagreement that already happened, and the reader that exists reads the weaker store. This repository's own 94 records carrying both stores and disagreeing are what that looks like.

The consequence is the migration D-50 already sized, not a surprise. 782 records carry the heading and 467 carry the field, so tightening the gate makes heading-only open records report what they owe. That is the correct reading of their state, and closed records keep the heading as evidence.
payload.title: make the kit gate read the field on an open record as D-50 already decided

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value: owed reads acceptance_criteria and requirements from the fields alone on an open record; a heading-only open record reports both as owed, and dor refuses it. A closed record still reads the heading as a fallback, so evidence already written stays readable. The trigger stays a heading, which D-50 keeps.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: The kit takes closedness as an argument rather than importing the vocabulary, so shaping stays a leaf module. No engine import, standard library only, Python 3.9 floor. Every caller passes the record's real status, because defaulting to open would mark 1020 closed records as owing. The engine seam must be able to write both fields before the gate reads only them.

## Context

Windows quality gate, run 33172159195 at c7f12113 (2026-08-28), after basicly-dufmjm and basicly-xyx556 cleared the two deterministic failures: `tests/test_supervise_board.py::test_one_emission_stays_inside_the_beat_it_rides` fails with `assert (1053.72 - 1050.61) < 3.0`. `EMIT_CAP_S` is `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_S / 5` = 3.0 s. The fixture emission measures 0.48 s on the author's machine and 3.1 s on the windows-latest runner: a wall-clock cap set at 6x the local figure does not clear a 6.5x slower CI file system. The module's own comment says the bound that governs is the beat the emission rides and the staleness horizon, not a fraction chosen for the fixture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the cap is set, IT SHALL be half the heartbeat (7.5 s), a bound that still fails on a 15x regression of the fixture figure and clears the slowest runner in the matrix by more than 2x.
- WHEN the test runs on windows-latest, macos-latest and ubuntu-latest, IT SHALL pass on all three in the same run.
- WHEN the comment above the cap is read, IT SHALL state the measured Windows figure and why the cap is half the beat.

## Scope

- `tests/test_supervise_board.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L1`
- demonstration: the `quality-gates` Windows job green on the landing commit, read from the job log.

payload.description:
Follow-up from the basicly-8z52 pilot (see docs/harness-eval.md). The pilot showed the skill-injection channel measurably changes behavior on a targeted discipline at trivial token cost, but was N=1, gates-off, and partly circular. Build the repeatable A/B eval so the whole-harness claim can be re-measured on demand.

Scope:
- A small fixed, versioned task set (5-8 tasks), each targeting one harness-enforced discipline, each shipping a HIDDEN objective check the arms never see (so a skill cannot trivially satisfy the scorer).
- A thin A/B driver: run each task under Arm H (harness: skills + gates + rework loop ON) vs Arm B (bare), reusing rubrics.evaluate() for C1-C4 and policy.rework_attempts for C5. No new telemetry.
- Pin a cheap model (Haiku) on both arms via RunnerSpec.model; reserve a strong model for judging; run across >=2 agent families (Claude, Copilot).
- Report per-criterion tables + arm totals; do not collapse to one number.

The key upgrade over the pilot: turn gates + rework ON for Arm H so the deterministic-gate and rework channels (the harness's largest claimed lift) are actually measured. Shares task-set and scorer plumbing with the per-skill eval basicly-4t9z; reuses the rubric primitive basicly-0122.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When the board renderer imports asset metadata, I want its dependency graph to exclude output writers, so I can preserve the existing renderer boundary while refusing linked export destinations.

## Steps to Reproduce

The integrated suite fails tests/test_board_render.py::test_the_renderer_imports_nothing_that_could_read_engine_state because board_assets now imports board_output. This is a real production dependency boundary violation. Repository callsite search finds only board_cli and tests call write_beside; no documented package contract requires that internal module location. The separate standalone board wheel was proven engine-free and serves HTML and API under Python -I -S; its source graph does not use these engine renderer modules.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_assets.py`
- `src/basicly/board_output.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `tests/test_board_render.py`
- `tests/test_board_output.py`
- `tests/test_board_assets.py`
- `.importlinter`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Repair Boundary

Move asset output writing into the existing board_output writer and keep board_assets as metadata and read helpers. Update every caller while preserving list returns, refusal reporting and safe atomic writes. Restore the actual pure renderer graph rather than allowing writer imports or escaping the AST check. Keep any guard strengthening focused on existing allowed runtime dependencies and concrete forbidden-import controls. Reorder the existing import layer and regenerate only its architecture block. No standalone kit or dependency changes are needed.

## Confirmation Plan

Run renderer boundary and all board output/asset/CLI/record tests. Exercise packaged export refusal controls and retain standalone board consumer proof.
payload.requirements: Preserve the existing dependency gate and all symlink refusal controls. Do not merely whitelist the writer or change import syntax to evade the test. Keep the standalone package engine independent.

payload.description:
## Context

Found by the lane-A and lane-E surveys independently, 2026-08-14. Verified by hand.

```text
dispatch_brief.py:31   VALIDATE_GATE = "validate-as-consumer"    zero consumers
validate_gate.py:31    VALIDATE_GATE = "validate-as-consumer"    every consumer uses this one
integrity.py:182       the string spelled a third time
```

Vulture cannot see the dead copy. `validate_gate`'s uses of its own constant mask `dispatch_brief`'s by bare name. That is the same masking mechanism `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py:166-170` already records for `CreatedChild.depends_on`.

## Why the third spelling matters most

`integrity.py:182` decides whether a unit requires validation at L3. If a rename reaches `validate_gate` and not `integrity`, then `requires_validation` silently stops requiring validation. That is a fail-open on the gate this repository added one day ago.

## The second half

`policy.GATE_TYPE_BY_GATE` (policy.py:93-108) is introduced as every gate the engine names, and its pinning test at `tests/test_policy.py:3184` enumerates a set that omits `validate-as-consumer`. The gate is engine-named, engine-recorded (validate_gate.py:125-146) and required at L3. It falls to the REVISION default, which happens to match the behaviour at loop.py:437. So this is a false completeness claim rather than a behaviour defect, and the claim is what the map exists for.

## Why the fix is legal today

`validate_gate.py:24` already imports `VERDICT_PREFIX` from `dispatch_brief`, its direct junior in `.importlinter:30-31`.

## Acceptance

- When the string `validate-as-consumer` is searched under `src/basicly/`, then exactly one definition site remains.
- When `policy.gate_type` is asked for that gate, then an explicit entry in `GATE_TYPE_BY_GATE` answers it, and the pinning test includes it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/dispatch_brief.py`
- `src/basicly/validate_gate.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/integrity.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
- `tests/test_validate_gate.py`

## Warning

`policy.py` has 10 tokens of size headroom. The dictionary entry must ride with a deletion or a comment trim in the same diff.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_policy.py tests/test_validate_gate.py -q` and `uv run basicly check`.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a write dispatch driven through the single-track loop path when its recorded occupancy crosses the resolved runners ceiling then the lane finalizes early and spins exactly one follow-up bead exactly as a supervised lane does and a test proves it red first against a stubbed low ceiling
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

```
rg -n "ceiling_tokens|OVERRUN_MARKER|existing_followup" src/basicly/loop.py src/basicly/supervise.py src/basicly/cli.py
uv run python -c "
import json, pathlib
r = json.loads(pathlib.Path('.basicly/usage/run-records.json').read_text())['basicly-23ep'][0]
print(r['phase'], r['forecast_tokens'], r['context_tokens'])"
```

Observed - `ceiling_tokens`, `OVERRUN_MARKER` and `existing_followup` occur **only** in
`supervise.py`, and the finalize protocol has exactly one call site: `supervise.py:2284`. Nothing in
`loop.py` or `cli.py` meters the context ceiling. Expected - a guard the design calls a behavioural
protection (factory design D8, section 7.6) applies on every write dispatch, not only the supervised
one.

## Context

`record_dispatch` calls `runner.context_occupancy` on both paths, so the *measurement* is taken
everywhere - which is why the evidence below exists at all. Only the supervised path *acts* on it.

**Measured on this bead's own parent.** `basicly-23ep` was driven single-track with
`basicly loop run basicly-23ep --root basicly-yc0x` on 2026-08-04. It recorded a context occupancy of
**403051 tokens** against the then-declared window of 200000 and its derived trigger of 120000 - 3.4x
the trigger - and was **neither finalized early nor given a follow-up bead**. It ran to completion and
committed normally. The guard simply was not there.

Two things follow, and the second is the reason this is filed separately from basicly-23ep:

1. **The twelve `(context-ceiling overrun)` follow-up beads all came from supervised passes.** The
   single-track path has been dispatching unmetered the whole time, so the truncation history is a
   property of one of the two write paths, not of the engine.
2. **The two paths disagree about a bead's fate for reasons unrelated to the bead.** The same work,
   at the same size, is truncated-and-followed-up under `supervise` and completed under `loop run`.
   That is a nondeterminism in the engine's own output, in the family basicly-jr0l's determinism
   critique tracks.

This is Phase S's shape exactly - **an instrument built and never connected** - and the same shape as
`permissions-check` shipping wired to no gate and the import contract reporting `1 kept, 0 broken`
forever. It belongs with basicly-uexy's wired-or-deleted gate, which would have caught it: the
finalize protocol's symbols have no caller outside their own module.

**Do not treat this as an argument for removing the ceiling.** basicly-23ep corrected the window to
1000000, which puts the trigger at 600000, and 403051 is comfortably under it - so the guard is
now plausible rather than punitive, and wiring it is safe in a way it was not this morning. Wire it,
or delete it and say so.

## Fix shape

- One metering site both write paths reach, rather than a second copy in `loop.py` - a duplicated
  ceiling is how the two paths came to disagree in the first place.
- The follow-up-spinning half (`existing_followup` and the `[harness-overrun]` marker) is already
  idempotent, so the single-track path can reuse it unchanged.
- A test that drives the **single-track** path past a stubbed-low ceiling and asserts the lane
  finalizes and spins exactly one follow-up, proven red first (basicly-kjc5.49). A test that only
  exercises `supervise` is what let this ship.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
payload.title: The context ceiling is inert on the single-track dispatch path

payload.description:
## Context

Owner review of the live wall 2026-08-21, after the layout redraw landed. The layout is honest and legible; what it is not is *designed for a wall*. Five findings, each a design fault rather than a defect:

1. **The altitude is wrong.** 36 gate checks named individually is a debugging view. From six metres the answer is one token. That block is roughly 15% of the screen carrying nothing actionable, and the name-overlap defect (`basicly-uvpu6b`) is a symptom of forcing it in.
2. **Every region has identical visual weight** - same border, same scale, same mint outline. A wall ranks by urgency; this ranks by nothing. The orange ask band works only because it is the sole exception.
3. **Dead space dominates.** IN FLIGHT is 40% of the viewport and empty most of the time, announcing nothing three times with dashed placeholders, while NEXT UP is squeezed into a narrow column truncating every title.
4. **There is no time axis.** Totals with no trend. A reader cannot tell whether the factory is improving, which is the question a wall exists to answer.
5. **`148h 26m` does not read at distance.** The number that matters is six days.

## The principle

**A green state costs one token; an exception expands.** Everything below follows from it.

## The layout

```text
status bar   one line: repo, gates as ONE token, spend, throughput, freshness
the alarm    ~64px. Age is the headline, the id and kind beneath it
the loop     seven counts AND a proportional bar, so 212 against 1 is visible
running now  one card per lane; collapses to ONE LINE when empty, giving its
             width to next up, which then stops truncating
backlog      one line: total, closed bar, per-priority
events       one line
```

## The five decisions

- **Gates collapse to a single token** - `GATES GREEN`, or `1 FAILING: pytest` with the failing names only. This deletes the overlap defect rather than patching it.
- **Age is the headline.** `6 DAYS` at wall scale, not `148h 26m`.
- **RUNNING NOW collapses when empty** to `no lane dispatched - last landed 4m ago`, and its space goes to NEXT UP.
- **The loop gets a proportional bar** beneath the counts.
- **One throughput figure** in the status bar - closed today, derived from `status` events, the only honest trend the ledger supplies cheaply.

## What must not be lost

Everything the current page gets right: the freshness sentence once, an absent section naming the producer that did not emit it, the section inventory from `board_schema.verdict` and never a second list, no external origin, a bar needing both its numbers, every state on two non-colour channels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN every gate passes, THE GATES REGION SHALL occupy one token; WHEN one fails, IT SHALL name the failing checks and only those.
- WHEN an ask is pending, ITS AGE SHALL be the largest text in that region, rendered in the coarsest honest unit.
- WHEN no lane is dispatched, THE RUNNING REGION SHALL occupy one line and the ready list SHALL take the reclaimed width.
- WHEN a ready title is rendered in the reclaimed width, THE TOP THREE SHALL NOT be truncated.
- WHEN the loop is rendered, EACH PHASE SHALL carry a bar proportional to its share of the active population.
- WHEN the ledger can supply it, THE STATUS BAR SHALL carry units closed today; WHERE it cannot, THE FIGURE SHALL be absent rather than zero.
- WHEN the page is measured, NEITHER the overflow instrument NOR the overlap instrument SHALL report anything at 1920x1080 or 1200x900.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/templates/board/*.j2`
- `src/basicly/board_wall.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `tests/test_board_wall.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_footer.py`
- `tests/test_board_render.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `220000`
- depends on: `basicly-uvpu6b`
- demonstration: The board rendered headless from this repository's own snapshot at 1920x1080 and 1200x900, with both instruments reporting nothing, and each acceptance criterion read off the screenshots rather than off the tests.

## Context

CONTRIBUTING.md section Development setup tells a new contributor to run `uv run pre-commit install --install-hooks -t pre-commit -t commit-msg -t pre-push`, commented as activating the git gates for all three stages. It does not.

Measured 2026-09-01 on a fresh clone of this repo, run in the clone own uv environment:

```text
$ pre-commit install --install-hooks -t pre-commit -t commit-msg -t pre-push
pre-commit installed at .git/hooks/pre-push
$ basicly hooks-check
Note: git hooks are not installed for stages: pre-push. Run `basicly hooks-build` ...
$ grep -c ledger .git/hooks/pre-push
0
```

The positive control, in the same clone:

```text
$ basicly hooks-build
Activated git hooks for stages: pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push.
$ basicly hooks-check          # no note
$ grep -c ledger .git/hooks/pre-push
5
```

So the documented command is the one `hooks-check` exists to warn about, and the warning names the fix the document does not. `hooks.py` already records the fact at `apply_pre_push_guard`: a bare `pre-commit install` rewrites the pre-push hook and drops the ledger guard.

`basicly hooks-check` prints its note on stderr and exits 0. That fail-open is deliberate - cli.py:1891 states that CI runs the scripts directly and does not install git hooks - so no gate refuses a clone that followed the document. A contributor gets a note they may not read and a pre-push stage that is missing its guard.

Reported by an operator whose colleague cloned this repo, started the board, and found the gates not installed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a contributor follows the Development setup block verbatim on a fresh clone, `basicly hooks-check` SHALL print no missing-stage note.
- WHEN the setup block names a command, THAT COMMAND SHALL be the one whose remedy `hooks-check` names.
- WHERE the pre-push ledger guard exists, THE DOCUMENT SHALL say that `pre-commit install` alone does not write it.

## Scope

- `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: L1
- demonstration: on a fresh clone, running the documented block then `basicly hooks-check` prints no note and `grep -c ledger .git/hooks/pre-push` is non-zero

payload.description:
## Context

Curating the v0.9.0 cut found **19 of the 54 beads closed since v0.8.0 carry no changelog.d fragment**, including basicly-4kdm - the seven specialist agents and five loop skills, which are vendored to every consumer by basicly install and are the single largest thing in the release.

The release body is a consumer surface. .github/workflows/release.yml extracts CHANGELOG.md from the **tagged** commit, so a missing fragment is unrecoverable after the tag: the note can never reach the published release. That is the same one-shot property basicly-m3od.1 already paid for from the other direction.

## Why nothing caught it

changelog.d refuses a fragment that is empty or misnamed, so the gate binds on **fragments that exist**. Nothing binds on a **closed bead that produced none**, and absence is exactly the shape a presence check cannot see. The eight fragments written by hand during the cut are the mopping, not the fix.

## What the check would be

A closed bead whose commits touched anything outside docs, tests and the tracker, with no matching changelog.d/<id>.<category>.md, is either a release note that was forgotten or a change that is genuinely invisible to a consumer - and the second case is a declaration, not a default. Ratchet it the way noqa-debt is ratcheted: freeze today's unaccounted set, fail on growth, so the backlog is not a blocker but a new omission is.

Note the discriminator problem this shares with basicly-r343 and the wired-or-deleted gate: bind the check on a marker the producer writes, because absence alone cannot tell a defect from a bead that predates the rule.

## Measured

- 54 beads closed since the v0.8.0 tag, 35 with a fragment, 19 without.
- Consumer-visible among the 19: 4kdm, u2hl.4, u2hl.11, u2hl.12, u2hl.13, u2hl.32, m4zv.6, a3ab.1, a3ab.12.
- Eight fragments were written by hand at cut time to close the gap for this release.
payload.title: a closed bead can ship with no release note and nothing notices

- Eight fragments were written by hand at cut time to close the gap for this release.

## Re-measured for the current cut, 2026-08-19

The figures above are the v0.8.0 to v0.9.0 window and stand as history. For the cut now pending:
**43 records closed since the v0.9.0 tag carry no changelog fragment, 22 of them user visible** - 19 bugs and 3 features, including make VALIDATE a real loop phase gated at L3 and make retrospective a state fired by a special cause signal. Both are ladder level capabilities that would ship with no release note. `release.blocking_reasons` has no check for it, so the omission is invisible to the gate that guards the cut.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. List the records closed since the most recent release tag.
2. List the fragment ids under `changelog.d/`.
3. Take the set difference and observe 43 closed records with no fragment.
4. Filter that difference to records typed bug or feature and observe 22.
5. Run the release gate predicates and observe `blocking_reasons` reports nothing about any of them.

Observed: a closed record that changed consumer visible behaviour can reach a tag with no release note, and the gate that guards the cut is silent.
Expected: the cut refuses, or the omission is declared, before the tag moves.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a record closed since the last tag whose commits touched anything outside docs and tests and the tracker, with no matching fragment, when the check runs then it fails and names the record.
- Given today's unaccounted set when the check first runs then it is frozen, so the existing backlog does not block a cut while a new omission does.
- Given a frozen entry that gains a fragment when the check runs then the entry is reported as graduated rather than left stale.
- Given a closed record whose change is genuinely invisible to a consumer when its author declares that then the check accepts the declaration and records it.
- Given the check is wired when the release gate runs then the omission appears in `blocking_reasons` rather than only in a report.
- Given a record that predates the rule when the check runs then it is not reported as a defect, because the check binds on a marker the producer writes.

## Scope

- `.scripts/`
- `src/basicly/release.py`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/`

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-07: *"to remove the error create a favicon.ico based on the logo on our basicly html page, so we no longer have the error in console log, and a nice icon in the browser tab."*

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `uv run basicly board serve --port 8787`
2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8787/` and read the browser console.

Observed: a failed request for `/favicon.ico`. Every board page shows the browser's blank-document glyph in its tab, so three open tabs - wall, loop and backlog - are indistinguishable.

## Why it is worth a record rather than a shrug

A console carrying a standing error is a console nobody reads, and the board's own debugging story is *read the console*. One permanent 404 trains a reader to ignore the pane where a real fault would appear.

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE SERVER SHALL answer `/favicon.ico` with an icon, so no board page logs a failed request for it.
- THE ICON SHALL be derived from the wordmark the board already draws, not a new mark invented here.
- WHERE the board is written by `board --out`, THE ICON SHALL be written beside the page so the file:// artifact carries it too.
- THE PAGE SHALL reference the icon with a relative path and no external origin.
- A TEST SHALL assert the route answers and that the bytes are a valid icon, not an empty file.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`

## Trigger

When a board page opens the browser requests a favicon that does not exist and logs an error, and I want a favicon served, so I can read the console for real defects instead of filtering a known one out every time.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-07: *"to remove the error create a favicon.ico based on the logo on our basicly html page, so we no longer have the error in console log, and a nice icon in the browser tab."*

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `uv run basicly board serve --port 8787`
2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8787/` and read the browser console.

Observed: a failed request for `/favicon.ico`. Every board page shows the browser's blank-document glyph in its tab, so three open tabs - wall, loop and backlog - are indistinguishable.

## Why it is worth a record rather than a shrug

A console carrying a standing error is a console nobody reads, and the board's own debugging story is *read the console*. One permanent 404 trains a reader to ignore the pane where a real fault would appear.

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE SERVER SHALL answer `/favicon.ico` with an icon, so no board page logs a failed request for it.
- THE ICON SHALL be derived from the wordmark the board already draws, not a new mark invented here.
- WHERE the board is written by `board --out`, THE ICON SHALL be written beside the page so the file:// artifact carries it too.
- THE PAGE SHALL reference the icon with a relative path and no external origin.
- A TEST SHALL assert the route answers and that the bytes are a valid icon, not an empty file.

## The defect

`.basicly/core/skills/work-tracker/skill.yaml` contradicts itself. Its Writes section at line 72 shows `basicly tracker write -- update <id> --add-label phase-7` as a working call and line 76 explains that it accumulates under the ledger lock. Its Refuses section at line 112 says the opposite:

> There is no owned label write. `update --add-label` (and every other label flag) raises at the seam ... Any instruction to label a record, a lane or a cut is therefore false: select work by id.

## Which half is true

The Writes section. Read 2026-08-18:
- `src/basicly/owned_write.py:53` `_resolve_labels` reads the record's own labels and rewrites the argv into `--labels` before translation, and line 117 documents the write as a read-modify-write under the lock.
- `src/basicly/owned_write.py:130` calls `mirror.drafts(kit_module, _resolve_labels(...))`, so the resolver always runs first.
- The raise at `src/basicly/mirror.py:117` is an internal guard on the un-resolved entry point. Its own message names the resolver that handles the case. A user never reaches it.

The false bullet is residue from before the label write landed under basicly-vkh0.42.

## Why it is priority 1

The consumer is a dispatched agent, not a human. The bullet does not merely confuse: it instructs the reader that every labelling instruction is false. `basicly loop supervise --label` is the multi-lane selection mechanism, so an agent that obeys this bullet refuses the parallel path. Nothing tests skill prose, so no gate sees it.

Given a reader of the work-tracker skill, then no passage states that a label write is refused, and the skill's Writes and Refuses sections do not contradict each other.

---

## 1. Canonical building blocks table

| # | Block | Purpose | Evidence | basicly coverage |

| 4 | **Code style — deltas from defaults only** | Only conventions that differ from tool/language defaults; delegate the rest to formatters | Anthropic include/exclude table ("code style rules that differ from defaults" vs "standard language conventions Claude already knows"); HumanLayer ("never send an LLM to do a linter's job"); awesome-claude-md ~66/109 | **COVERED** — `python-style` (path-scoped rule, 3 bullets, points at `ruff format` pre-commit hook). payload.description:
The two most-corroborated blocks (every source puts them first) are missing from the core scaffold: a project-overview fragment (purpose in 1-2 lines, stack with versions, entry points, pointer to architecture docs — NOT an embedded directory map, per Anthropic /doctor trim guidance) and a commands fragment whose body is fenced, verbatim-runnable command groups (setup/test/single-test/lint). install should scaffold per-repo overlay stubs for both so every consumer starts with them.

## Design

Content is inherently per-repo, so these land as install-scaffolded overlay stubs (written once when absent, never overwritten — same contract as tasks.json/basicly-gates.yml), created as status: draft so placeholder text never pollutes projections (planner filters to active); the consumer fills them in and flips to active. This repo dogfoods by authoring real, active versions in its own overlay.

## Acceptance Criteria

- basicly install scaffolds .basicly-local/fragments/user/project/project-overview.fragment.yaml and .basicly-local/fragments/user/commands/commands.fragment.yaml when absent, with draft status and a fill-me structure (overview: purpose, stack, entry points, docs pointer; commands: fenced setup/test/single-test/lint groups).
- Existing files at those paths are never overwritten on re-install.
- Scaffolded stubs load as valid fragments (catalog-lint passes with them present) and, being draft, do not change projections until activated.
- Unit tests cover: scaffold-when-absent, no-overwrite, stub validity.
- Dogfood: this repo's overlay gains real active project-overview and commands fragments; projections regenerated; all checks green.

payload.description:
Git hooks gate only at commit time; Anthropic's model gates at tool time (PreToolUse, exit 2 blocks) and turn end (Stop). Add a projection of agent-native hooks into .claude/settings.json, starting with a protect-files guard for generated outputs (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions.md, rules/instructions files, projected skills) — the do-not-edit-generated-files rule currently lives only in prose. Tier-1 curated pattern (Pydantic's DO NOT EDIT blocks).

## Design

- New stdlib-only script .basicly/core/hooks/protect-generated.py: reads the PreToolUse JSON payload from stdin, extracts tool_input.file_path, and exits 2 (block, stderr shown to the model with the edit-the-source alternative) when the target file carries a 'Generated by ... basicly' marker in its first lines or is the generated manifest json; fails open on malformed input or missing files.
- hooks.yaml entries gain an optional manager field (default git); the new hook is manager claude, stage pretooluse. Git-side rendering (pre-commit config, stage installation) filters to manager git.
- claude_settings.py gains merge/check functions that project manager-claude hooks into the hooks.PreToolUse section of the committed .claude/settings.json (matcher Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit), preserving all consumer keys and any foreign hooks; idempotent by managed command match.
- hooks-build applies the settings projection; hooks-check reports drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Editing a marker-carrying generated file through Edit/Write is blocked by the hook script (exit 2) with a message naming the catalog source workflow; normal files pass; malformed payloads fail open.
- basicly hooks-build writes the PreToolUse wiring into .claude/settings.json without disturbing existing settings; re-running is a no-op; hooks-check flags a removed or altered managed entry.
- pre-commit config and git stage installation are unchanged by the new manager field (git hooks keep working; agent hooks never reach pre-commit).
- Unit tests cover the script verdicts, the settings merge/check, and the manager filtering.
- Dogfood: this repo's .claude/settings.json gains the wiring via hooks-build; piping a synthetic PreToolUse payload for CLAUDE.md into the script blocks it.

## Context

Observed 2026-08-26, basicly-zq9i2m round 1, supervisor log: `routed: basicly-j7spdb -> error - routing failed: a gate refused git commit -m chore(beads): sync tracker state for the harness loop (basicly-j7spdb): pre-commit-script refused: [tester] WARNING nosec encountered (B607) ... Contracts: 3 kept, 0 broken.` Then `routed: basicly-pjaudy -> held - landing paused after an earlier failure this pass` and the same for basicly-1djm17. Round 2 re-dispatched basicly-j7spdb to an implementer although its branch held 2 commits on a clean tree. `uv run basicly verify --mode fast` in base 20 minutes later: 34/34 pass. Three defects in one chain:

1. `checkout._failure` (`src/basicly/checkout.py:117-131`) hands the joined hook output to `gate_refusal`, which returned the bandit `nosec` warnings and the import-linter summary instead of the `FAILED: <check>` line and the `checks failed: N/M` summary. The operator cannot tell which gate refused a ledger-only commit, so the cause stays unknown.
2. `supervise.route_outcomes` (`src/basicly/supervise.py:3055-3062`) turns any RuntimeError from `_route_one` into route `error`, and the next pass treats an `error` lane as work to dispatch. A landing that failed on the engine's own tracker-sync commit is not a lane defect; it needs the landing retried, not an agent (~8M tokens, the basicly-pjaudy shape).
3. `landing_blocked` then holds every later green lane for the rest of the pass. That is right for a lane defect that could poison the base, and wrong for an infra refusal the next attempt would clear.

## Steps to Reproduce

Make the tracker-sync pre-commit refuse once (for example a hook that fails on its first call and passes on the second), run a supervise pass with three green lanes. Observed: lane 1 routed `error` with no gate name, lanes 2 and 3 `held`, lane 1 re-dispatched next pass. Expected: the refusal names the check, the tracker-sync commit is retried once, and a committed lane is never re-dispatched over a landing-side refusal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an engine-run `git commit` is refused by a hook, THE ERROR SHALL name the failing check from the `FAILED:` line and carry the `checks failed: N/M` summary, and SHALL NOT be built from warning lines alone.
- WHEN the tracker-sync commit is refused and the refusing check passes on an immediate re-run, THE LANDING SHALL continue in the same pass, and the pass narrative SHALL record the retry and the check.
- WHEN a landing fails on the engine's own commit rather than on the lane's diff, THE LANE SHALL keep route `ready to land` for the next pass and SHALL NOT be dispatched to an agent.
- WHEN a landing fails on the lane's diff, THE HELD RULE SHALL apply as today.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/checkout.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_checkout.py`
- `tests/test_merge_ledger.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

payload.description:
MEASURED 2026-09-13. Five live `claude -p --output-format json` dispatches from the repository root, so each loaded the real project context. Total cost of the experiment: $0.9435 at list price.

DESIGN. Three comparable read-only tasks, each two files of about 9-11 KB, each asking for a count of level-2 headings. Task A seeded a session. Task B and task C were then each run twice: once in a fresh session, once resumed into the session that already held the earlier tasks. Same prompt, same files, same model, same permissions. The only variable is whether the session was warm.

RESULT.

| run | turns | cache_read | cache_write | total tokens | cost $ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A fresh, 1st | 2 | 33,750 | 34,081 | 68,166 | 0.3670 |
| B fresh | 2 | 46,646 | 21,093 | 68,037 | 0.2426 |
| B warm, 2nd in session | 2 | 68,422 | 556 | 69,301 | 0.0478 |
| C fresh | 2 | 46,658 | 21,100 | 67,933 | 0.2396 |
| C warm, 3rd in session | 2 | 69,514 | 546 | 70,313 | 0.0465 |

Task B warm/fresh: cost **0.20x**, tokens 1.02x. Task C warm/fresh: cost **0.19x**, tokens 1.04x.

**A warm worker costs about five times less per task than a fresh one, at the same token count.** Two independent replications, same direction, same magnitude.

THE MECHANISM, AND WHY A TOKEN COUNT HIDES IT. The totals are the same to within 4%. What moves is the split: cache_write falls from about 21,000 to about 550, a 97% drop, and cache_read rises to match. A cache **write** is billed at a premium over base input and a cache **read** at a deep discount, so relocating the same tokens from write to read is the whole saving. **Any cost argument conducted in tokens rather than in priced components is wrong**, and one conducted in this repository on 2026-09-13 was wrong for exactly that reason.

ACCUMULATION DID NOT ERODE IT. The third task in the session performed the same as the second, 0.19x against 0.20x, while the carried prefix grew only 1.5%, from 69,301 to 70,313. The prior claim that a long-lived worker grows the dominant cost term is refuted at this scale.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH.
- n=2 replications, two turns per task. The mechanism is a price split rather than a task-size effect, so the direction should hold, but the magnitude on a 26-turn lane is not measured. A long task amortises its single cache write over more turns in the fresh arm too, so 5x is likely an upper bound.
- Every run was seconds after its predecessor, so the cache was always hot. The `cache_creation` block reports `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`, so this path writes a one-hour cache; a subagent defaults to five minutes unless `subagentPromptCacheTtl` is set to `1h`.
- The tasks only read. A task that writes files grows the conversation faster, so a longer-lived worker may reach a compaction threshold that these three did not.

THE DESIGN CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS A SCHEDULING RULE RATHER THAN A LIFETIME POLICY. A warm worker is cheap only while its cache is hot. A worker that idles past the TTL re-writes an accumulated and therefore larger prefix at full price, which is worse than starting fresh. So: **keep a worker busy inside the TTL, or let it end.** An idle warm worker is the worst case in the system.

That rule unifies two parts of the proposed factory that looked independent. A pull queue in which a free worker takes the next ready task immediately is precisely the mechanism that keeps a warm worker inside its cache window. **The kanban is not a convenience on top of the worker pool. It is what makes the worker pool economic.**

RAW DATA. Five result objects retained under the session scratchpad as `r1_A_fresh.json`, `r2_B_fresh.json`, `r3_B_warm.json`, `r5_C_fresh.json`, `r4_C_warm3.json`. Reproduce with `claude -p "<task>" --allowedTools Read --output-format json [--resume <id>]` and read `total_cost_usd` and `usage` from each.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a seat becomes free, I want it to take the next ready task that matches it, so I can keep it inside its cache window without a separate scheduler deciding when to hand work over.

## Requirements

R1. Work is never pushed to a seat, because a seat that is not running cannot receive it.
R2. Two seats never take the same task.
R3. A seat takes its next task fast enough to stay inside the cache window, or it is released.
R4. The order tasks are taken in is the order the existing ranked ready set already publishes, so this adds no second scheduler.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a seat reports free and a matching ready task exists, then it is assigned that task without a new spawn. [check: `tests/test_seat_queue.py`]
- When two seats report free at the same moment, then each takes a different task and neither takes one twice. [check: `tests/test_seat_queue.py`]
- When no ready task matches a free seat, then the seat is released rather than held idle. [check: `tests/test_seat_queue.py`]
- When a task is taken, then the five admission conditions and the six admission gates have all been applied first. [check: `tests/test_supervise_admission.py`]

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_seat_queue.py -q`

## Design notes

Architecture section 31A.3. This is not a second scheduler: the ready set already ranks and section 28.2's five conditions are already the pull predicate. What changes is who spawns.

- R4. The order tasks are taken in is the order the existing ranked ready set already publishes, so this adds no second scheduler.

## CORRECTED 2026-08-13 — read this before the text below
The defect is real and shipping: `runner.py:151` still ships `claude: 200_000` and a consumer
with no `[runner] context_windows` inherits it. **Two things below are now wrong.**

**The remedy changed.** `implementation-plan.md:223` records the premise corrected 2026-08-09:
the binary reports its own window on the stream as `modelUsage.<id>.contextWindow`, so the fix
is to *read* it, not to ship a second hand-maintained constant. Nothing in `src/` reads that
field today - `runner.py:1794` reads `modelUsage` for model names only. **Acceptance criterion
1 below is therefore the wrong shape**: "assert the resolved window is not 200_000" pins a
second hand-written constant, which `factory-loop.md` section 15.6 forbids in the same breath
as deleting the ceiling.

**Its blocking consumer is being deleted.** Section 15.6 and D23 remove the context ceiling
outright: "a gate that has never once fired correctly - first at a fifth of its intended
point, then never - is removed rather than given a third constant." That is `basicly-u2hl.30`,
still open. Sequence this after it, at which point this bead narrows to the window declaration
and its provenance alone - which the bead's own text already concedes.

**The evidence needs replacing, and the replacement is stronger.** The "0 of 106 fire" figure
is unrefreshed. Measured over 346 records on 2026-08-13: `context_window_source` is
`{null: 220, "[runner] context_windows": 124, "conservative fallback": 2}` - the
**`adapter default` label appears zero times**, against a positive control where two other
labels do populate. So the shipped constant is unexercised *here*, which is precisely why it
reaches consumers unnoticed. Provenance recording is already built (`runner.py:158-161`,
`run_record.py:200-209`).

**Prerequisite:** `basicly-i4gg` (closed 2026-08-13) landed the envelope parse this remedy
reads from.

---

## Context

`basicly-23ep` fixed the claude context window after a stale `200_000` constant put the
finalize trigger at `120_000` and truncated healthy lanes for months — **18 follow-up beads
carrying `(context-ceiling overrun)`** are the recorded cost, and 51 of 79 lanes crossed
the wrong threshold.

**The fix reached this repo's config and nothing else** [M, 2026-08-08]:

```text
basicly.toml:568-569        [runner.context_windows]
                            claude = 1_000_000        <- this repo only
src/basicly/runner.py:142   _CONTEXT_WINDOWS = {"claude": 200_000, "codex": 400_000,
                                                "copilot": 128_000}   <- what SHIPS
```

`basicly` installs its harness into other repositories. A consumer that installs it and
does not hand-write a `[runner.context_windows]` override inherits `200_000`, so their
ceiling sits at `120_000` and truncates their lanes exactly as ours were truncated — the
defect `23ep` closed, still live for everyone but us.

## Why this is the sharpest form of a rule already in the plan

`implementation-plan.md` section 10: *"A constant describing an external capability must be
falsifiable against our own ledger. It is the one class of value that is correct when
written and rots silently as the vendor ships."* `23ep` added
`runner.window_violations` to make the **declaration** falsifiable — but it is falsifiable
against *this* repo's ledger, and the shipped default is the thing no ledger checks.

So this is not "update a number". Pasting `1_000_000` into `runner.py` is the same
unchecked declaration one generation on, and `23ep`'s own bead says so: *"Do not re-fix by
writing a bigger constant."* The adapter default needs either provenance and a staleness
check of its own, or it needs to stop being a silent default at all — e.g. refuse to meter
a ceiling when no window is declared for an agent, rather than assuming one.

## The second half: the ceiling is now inert here

Measured the same day: `ceiling_tokens(claude) = 600_000` against a maximum observed
occupancy of `403_051` over 106 metered dispatches, so **0 of 106 fire**. The gate has gone
from firing at one fifth of its intended point to being unreachable, and **neither state has
ever been correct**. `basicly-u2hl.30` deletes the ceiling on exactly that ground. If it
lands first, this bead narrows to the window declaration alone; if it does not, a consumer
still carries the mis-firing version.

## Steps to Reproduce

```text
$ grep -n '_CONTEXT_WINDOWS' src/basicly/runner.py
142:_CONTEXT_WINDOWS = {"claude": 200_000, "codex": 400_000, "copilot": 128_000}

$ grep -n -A1 'runner.context_windows' basicly.toml
568:[runner.context_windows]
569-claude = 1_000_000
```

Observed: a fresh consumer repo with no override meters claude at a 200,000 window.
Expected: a consumer inherits a window that is either correct or explicitly undeclared,
never a stale value presented as a default.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a consumer repo with no `[runner.context_windows]` override, when a claude
  dispatch is metered, then it does not use a window smaller than the model's real one
  - check: a test loads config from a fixture repo carrying no override and asserts the
  resolved claude window is not `200_000`.
- Given any agent whose window is not declared with provenance, when the ceiling would be
  metered, then the engine records that it could not meter rather than assuming a default
  - check: a test asserts the unmetered case is recorded and named, not silently defaulted.
- Given the shipped defaults, when they drift from the vendor's published windows, then
  something fails - check: a test or gate that reads the declaration's recorded provenance
  and fails when it is absent or older than the declared staleness bound.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly usage --json` in a fresh consumer repo with no override reports the claude
window it will meter against, and that value is not `200_000`.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly worktree merge` rebases a branch before merging it, so the original branch ref never becomes
an ancestor of base. `basicly worktree cleanup` tests ancestry, therefore reports **every** correctly
merged worktree as unmerged and tells the operator to re run with `--force`.

Measured 2026-08-20: after `basicly-rn0o.10` merged cleanly at `208616cb`, cleanup reported
`kept branch harness/basicly-rn0o.10 and its record (unmerged - re-run with force to reclaim)`, while
`git diff harness/basicly-rn0o.10 main` showed the content identical.

**A check that is wrong every time trains the operator to pass `--force` without reading it**, and
`--force` is what deletes an unmerged branch. In this session that habit came within one command of
discarding a commit that genuinely was not in base: `git diff branch main` showed main *removing* 92
lines, and only that diff caught it. The content check is the one that carries the information; the
ancestry check carries none.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a worktree with `basicly worktree create <name>` and commit on it.
2. Land it with `basicly worktree merge <name> --bead <id>` and observe MERGED.
3. Run `basicly worktree cleanup <name>`.
4. Observe it reports the branch as unmerged and offers `--force`.
5. Run `git diff <branch> main` and observe the tracked content is identical, so the report is false.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a worktree whose content is in base when cleanup runs then it reclaims the session without --force - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_worktree.py -k rebase_merged -q`
- Given a worktree carrying content base does not hold when cleanup runs then it refuses and names the differing paths rather than offering a blanket force

## Scope

- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `tests/test_worktree.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `tests/test_worktree.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_worktree.py -k rebase_merged -q`
payload.title: the worktree cleanup merge check is always wrong after a rebase merge so it trains its own bypass

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the build factor gap is classified then the record says whether the seeds or the scope read-cost they multiply is the wrong half, with the evidence that separates them, and any change to a factor is applied by a human to basicly.toml rather than by the tuner.
payload.description:
## Context

Surfaced by `basicly usage tuning` at session close, 2026-08-14, over 359 recorded dispatches.
Every per-class build factor in force is a **declared seed** and every one is far below what the
ledger measured:

```text
class   in force        advised (measured)   samples
bug     2   x scope     10.66                n=37
chore   1.5 x scope     11.93                n=10
task    3   x scope     17.25                n=27
```

Three classes, 74 samples, all `measured` rather than `seeded`, so each is past
`[policy.sizing] calibration_min_samples`. The smallest gap is 5.3x and the largest is 8.0x.

## Why this matters more than a mis-tuned constant

`architecture.md` §12.8.2 records that **nothing measures a working-set factor** - the calibration
that appeared to was measuring whole-lane spend, a different quantity, and was removed
(`basicly-z2wi`). So every forecast in the engine today is a declared constant times a scope
read-cost, and the record says so via `forecast_source`.

This is the first time the ledger has been able to answer what those constants should be, and the
answer is that they are systematically low by most of an order of magnitude. A forecast that low
feeds `supervise.admit_pass_spend`, the band, and every budget minted from a preflight.

## What this bead is NOT

It is **not** "apply the recommendation". `basicly usage tuning` is advisory by design and
changes no config, and `basicly.toml` is on the confirmation list. The tuner also warns that its
sample includes beads that never landed.

What is owed first is the classification the number needs: whether the 5-8x gap is the seeds being
wrong, or the scope read-cost the factor multiplies being wrong, or both. Those call for different
fixes and the ratio alone cannot separate them.

## Evidence

`uv run basicly usage tuning`, rows `policy.sizing.build_factor.{bug,chore,task}`.
payload.title: the declared build factors under-forecast a lane by three to eleven times

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the finding-set ledger has entries from real rework rounds when the trade rate and the eventual outcome of those lanes are counted then a decision is recorded on whether a traded finding set is a stalled round or progress and either the threshold changes with tests or basicly-m4zv.5 Context sentence is corrected to match the landed behaviour
payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-06 by exercising `basicly-m4zv.5` from base after it merged, rather than by
reading its tests. The landed behaviour satisfies the acceptance criterion and contradicts
one sentence of the same bead's Context, so the AC passing hid a design question.

`basicly-m4zv.5`'s Context says:

> Compare the open-finding set between consecutive iterations, not the count - **a round that
> fixes one finding and introduces one is not progress.**

The landed implementation disagrees. Measured against base at 4cbc777:

```
history [{pytest, ruff}]  now {pytest, vulture}
  verdict=progressing  rounds=0  -> keep spending
```

`policy._compare_finding_sets` returns `STALLED` only on set identity and `DIVERGING` only on a
strict superset; everything else is `PROGRESSING`. A trade is neither, so it falls through and
the round keeps spending its cap. There is a test asserting exactly this -
`test_a_finding_set_that_traded_one_finding_for_another_is_progressing` - so it is a decision,
not an oversight.

## Which is right is genuinely open

The AC only ever defined three cases - unchanged once, unchanged twice, grows - and a trade is
none of them, so **the implementation is correct against the AC**. The question is whether the
AC was complete.

**For the landed behaviour (trade = progressing).** Fixing `ruff` while `vulture` newly fails is
real movement, and a lane that clears findings one per round is the normal shape of iterative
work. Escalating it would ask a human about a lane that is working, and at `[policy] max_rework
= 2` there is almost no room for a lane to be wrong once. The rework cap already bounds a lane
that thrashes forever, so nothing is unbounded either way.

**For the Context sentence (trade = stalled).** The count is unchanged and the *quality* is
unknown; a lane that trades a finding every round never converges and burns its whole cap
before the cap notices. That is the same failure this bead's parent exists to stop, one level
subtler.

**A third reading, which may be what the sentence meant.** The sentence's job may be to argue
against comparing *counts* - "a count cannot tell a trade from real progress, so compare sets" -
rather than to fix the verdict for a trade. Under that reading nothing is wrong and this bead
closes as already-satisfied with the sentence clarified.

## What would settle it

Telemetry, not argument. `policy.record_finding_set` now writes a `[harness-policy] finding-set`
marker on every rework round, so the data accrues from here on: count how often consecutive
rounds trade rather than shrink, and whether those lanes eventually landed or escalated. A trade
that usually precedes a landing is progress; one that usually precedes an escalation is a stall.
Decide from the ledger the way `basicly-m4zv.14` settled the `-n auto` question, and do not
change the threshold before the ledger has entries.

## Steps to Reproduce

```sh
uv run python -c "
from basicly import policy
A = policy.finding_signature(['pytest','ruff'])
B = policy.finding_signature(['pytest','vulture'])
print(policy._compare_finding_sets([A], B))"
```

Prints `('progressing', ('pytest','ruff'), 0)`. Expected, if the Context sentence governs, is a
stalled verdict.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`

## Context

Measured 2026-08-20 at the end of a nine lane pass. Two test modules are at or within two tokens of
their effective size baseline:

- `tests/test_handoff.py` - frozen at 6302 with 0 tokens of headroom. `basicly-09lc5o` predicted its cut
  violation tests would move out and relieve it; they did not, because their consumer surface is
  `handoff.entry_verdict` and the receiving test module was outside that record's scope.
- `tests/test_validate_gate.py` - 3998 of 4000, two tokens. The lane that filled it attempted two splits
  and reverted both: cutting the verdict section breaks the `-k emphasis` demonstration an acceptance
  criterion names, and cutting the gate naming section yields a 59.6 percent density file needing a
  waiver, because that section is prose heavy evidence hidden inside a low density module.

`basicly-agzx.4` already names the general defect - a test module frozen at exactly its own size admits
no further test. This record carries the two live instances and the fact that both cheap splits have
already been tried and measured, so the next lane does not repeat them.

The decision this needs is deliberate rather than in lane: a split that moves a demonstration command has
to move the acceptance criterion with it, and a split needing a density waiver trades one ratchet for the
other.

- Given the two named test modules then each is under its size baseline with room for a further test and neither took a density waiver to get there - check: `uv run python .scripts/check_module_size.py`
- Given a split moves a test an acceptance criterion names then that record's demonstration command is updated in the same diff
- Given the split is complete then any frozen entry that reaches zero is deleted rather than left licensing regrowth
